text:
maya singh: Pushed a new runtime config were calling the 'low-latency wave' to prod canary. Targets small-sequence workloads (<64 tokens). Early canary numbers look good: p50 down ~18%, p99 down ~6%, unit cost ~-6%. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/rlw-bench

deploy-bot: Canary deployment completed on 120 hosts at 1718800020. No degradation alerts during smoke checks.

sam wu: Awesome — can you share the canary size + whats moving next?

maya singh: Canary initial = 5% traffic. We bumped to 25% this morning, moving to 50% in ~30m if no regressions. Plan to go to 100% over 24h if metrics hold. Baseline (conv-ens): p50 -18%, p95 -7%, small uptick in short-job GPU util.

leo herrera: Any infra-level changes I should call out in docs (KV cache / batching)?

maya singh: Yes — changes are infra-only: lowered coalescing window and enabled microkernel fastpath for short sequences. KV TTLs unchanged, but we enabled prefix-dedup for short prompts. Snippet of rollout config: ```runtime.policy.fastpath.enabled=true
runtime.policy.fastpath.seq_threshold=64
runtime.batch.coalesce_ms=8```

jordan (prod): Rolling criteria? Who's oncall for watching error budgets?

maya singh: Rollback conditions: p99 latency increase >5% vs baseline OR error-rate spike >0.2% sustained for 10m. Oncall team pinged. @oncall please monitor /prod/low-latency-wave and error budget dashboards.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout to 50% started at 1718800060.

sam wu: Quick numbers from staging runs: baseline p50 42ms -> 34.5ms, baseline p99 220ms -> 205ms. Cost per 1k tokens ~6.1% lower.

leo herrera: :tada: Nice. Any user-visible behavior changes?

maya singh: No API changes. Everything is behind the same endpoints. Users should see fewer timeouts on short queries and slightly faster responses.

support-bot: Support channels notified and a short note drafted for the status page; will update if needed.

sam wu: We should highlight this in the next all-hands (1-2 bullets).

maya singh: Agreed — I'll add a short blurb and link to the benchmark notebook. @marketing can you help craft a one-line callout for the all-hands slide?

marketing: Got it, will draft a line and drop it in #all-hands-draft by EOD.

jordan (prod): Thanks everyone. If no regressions, proceed to 100% over next 24h. I'll keep the rollout plan open in case we need to throttle.

maya singh: Thanks team — huge props to infra + runtime for the microkernel work. Will post a follow-up with the final 24h numbers.
